result:
The review of the `review` branch against `main` (the two commits redirecting cache/analytics writes to `/tmp` on Vercel and extracting the `dataDir()` helper) is complete. All 8 finder angles ran, I deduplicated their pools, verified code claims against the actual diff, and confirmed the two external Vercel platform claims with a web-sourced adversarial check against Vercel's docs and CLI source.

**10 findings reported — 9 confirmed, 1 plausible.** The two most consequential: the `process.env.VERCEL` truthiness check also fires in local dev after a routine `vercel env pull .env.local` (which writes `VERCEL="1"` by default), silently redirecting local writes to `/tmp`; and the new comment points to a "Deploy to Vercel" README section that doesn't exist — five of eight finders independently hit that one. The rest cover per-instance `/tmp` making Vercel analytics inconsistent (not just cold-start-ephemeral), unnamespaced `/tmp/cache` / `/tmp/analytics.jsonl` collision risk, a missing unit test for the new helper, no `DATA_DIR` escape hatch for other read-only hosts, and smaller cleanups.

Worth noting on the clean side: the cross-file trace found no broken call sites, no other code writing outside `dataDir()`, and byte-identical behavior for non-Vercel environments; the pre-existing sync-fs patterns in `persist.ts` were flagged by the efficiency finder but fall outside this diff, so I excluded them. Many of the findings would collapse together under one fix — a namespaced `os.tmpdir()`-based path with a `DATA_DIR` override and a runtime-specific Vercel guard — if you want, I can apply that plus the doc/test gaps.
